title: Cult-Like Cultures
coreMove: Make belonging conditional on lived values, so culture selects for fit instead of merely welcoming talent.
sourcePressure: The source supports strong membership defined by shared values and purpose beyond formal activity, with culture organized around real value alignment.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Confusing cult-like culture with perks, friendliness, conformity, or blind obedience, rather than clear standards that people freely join or leave.

sourceAnchors.name: shared values and purpose
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar supports strong membership defined by shared values and purpose beyond formal activity
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A strong culture is warm only to the people willing to live its standards.

hook: a strong culture is like a family
examples: sales star laughs at service oath

exampleSpecs.domain: aviation maintenance shop deciding whether to keep its fastest mechanic after skipped signoffs
exampleSpecs.audience: Laura, maintenance chief protecting a safety culture
exampleSpecs.stakes: one skipped signoff can ground aircraft or hide a defect
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Laura places the mechanic's speed metrics beside unsigned inspection cards and removes him from lead rotation until the standard is lived
exampleSpecs.firstImage: unsigned inspection cards clipped to a propeller cart
mustAvoid: talent versus culture as a speech

exampleSpecs.domain: software support team hiring a brilliant engineer who mocks customer callbacks
exampleSpecs.audience: Jack, support director filling a painful vacancy
exampleSpecs.stakes: one toxic expert could teach the team that customer patience is optional
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "I do not call users back," the candidate says, and Jack ends the interview despite the perfect technical score
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a technical scorecard with one line crossed out in black ink

exampleSpecs.domain: fire station probation process testing whether recruits reset gear for the next crew
exampleSpecs.audience: Lars, captain evaluating a high-performing recruit
exampleSpecs.stakes: individual bravery means little if the next crew inherits missing gear
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lars watches the recruit walk past an empty oxygen slot after a perfect drill and uses that visible miss as the membership test
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the rubber smell of masks drying beside an empty oxygen slot

exampleSpecs.domain: boutique hotel front desk enforcing guest-recovery rituals for senior hires
exampleSpecs.audience: Juliette, general manager onboarding an industry veteran
exampleSpecs.stakes: a veteran's polish can mask refusal to practice the hotel's recovery standard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Juliette two complaint cards to see the veteran was charming guests but skipping the handwritten recovery note, so she makes the ritual nonnegotiable
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two complaint cards tucked under a brass desk bell

exampleSpecs.domain: mutual-aid kitchen deciding whether a popular volunteer can ignore cleanup duty
exampleSpecs.audience: Sam, shift lead with a line outside
exampleSpecs.stakes: the kitchen's dignity standard frays if celebrity volunteers avoid ordinary work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sam reviews the shift after the volunteer left greasy trays, then changes the roster so service and cleanup are paired for everyone
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Who belongs in a kitchen where applause excuses the sink?

exampleSpecs.domain: design apprenticeship requiring critique participation before portfolio praise
exampleSpecs.audience: Catarina, studio founder choosing the next apprentice cohort
exampleSpecs.stakes: beautiful portfolios can hide people who cannot accept or give exacting critique
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Catarina ignore the prettiest portfolio until the applicant marks up another student's draft with care and precision
exampleSpecs.firstImage: portfolio boards leaning against a wall beside red critique stickers
mustAvoid: artistic taste as the whole filter

skillTargets: identify culture as enforced membership standards
choose fit tests that show values in action
separate exclusion for standards from exclusion for sameness

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one value your team claims. Write the behavior that proves it, the behavior that violates it, and what will happen the next time either appears.
sourceAnchorsNote: Frozen source sidecars for this book expose concept support and source artifacts, but little chapter-level anecdote detail after chapter 1. Use only the anchors listed here; do not invent company histories, named executives, studies, or dates.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
